title: Providers whose equipment orders stand far from their specialty
question: Which Bay Area providers order far more Medicare-paid equipment per patient than others in their specialty, or send large orders to only one or two suppliers?
finding: Of 5,983 Bay Area providers whose equipment orders Medicare paid in 2024, 40 ordered $150,000 or more at five times or more the per-patient middle figure for their specialty; most are Neurology (8), Nurse Practitioner (7), Orthopedic Surgery (4). 7 ordered $150,000 or more through only one or two suppliers. In 4 cases the provider who orders is also the supplier, or shares a street address with a supplier of the same item: Alexander Sah, MD, Fremont ($1.8 million); Bryant Bonner, MD, Fremont ($168,560); Mher Vartivarian, D.P.M., San Francisco ($186,662).
how: From the federal file of equipment and supplies by referring provider, 2024. Dollars are Medicare payments to suppliers for items the provider ordered. Each provider's payment per patient is set against the middle Bay Area provider of the same specialty (specialties with ten or more providers). Listed: $150,000 or more ordered, and either five times the specialty figure or only one or two suppliers. The note marks providers who also appear as the supplier, or who share a street address with an organization supplier of their main item.
limits: A specialist in a few costly conditions orders costly items, and for the highest rows the main item is a drug paid under the equipment benefit (the item column names it). A specialty clinic can stand far from its specialty's middle for that reason alone. Nurse practitioners and physician assistants are compared with all others of their profession, whatever clinic they work in. The provider who orders is not paid for the item unless the note says the supplier is at the same address. Patient counts under 11 are withheld.
